LLMs still produce bugs, but those bugs are different than what they used to be. It’s less off-by-ones and more about system design, ui usability, missing broader context. Some kinds of coding has been solved, but not all.

While models continue to improve, adversarial code review has been an incredibly powerful tool to catch many of these kinds of bugs.

It can be as simple as a one line prompt - “use a dynamic workflow to adversarial test every edge case in an iOS simulator”, or use Claude’s built in /code-review (or /code-review low, /code-review medium, etc.)
@swyx Worktrees can be rough when they pile up. I use a loop to clean up stale worktrees. Should we build this into Claude Code?
@PawelHuryn Have you tried /code-review low? From our evals, this produces a better result than other models at a fraction of the cost (<$0.01)

Closing the loop: this is now fully resolved. The issue was a server-side config change that caused the UI to show overages rather than subscriptions in some cases. In all cases, even though the UI showed overages, we correctly drew from your regular rate limits on the backend.

We also found that 196 people paid for Fable overages while experiencing this bug. If you are one of these people, in case the purchase was accidental, we have fully refunded your Fable credits. We also credited your accounts with extra overages as a thank you.

Keep the feedback coming! 🙏
@jadenitripp Each model generation requires less tokens to do the same task. As models improve, the Pareto-frontier shifts left, which means less tokens over time for the same task.
